bechacant.project: A social app built around challenges between users: a Next.js PWA with LLM features that also runs inside the iOS and Android apps.
bechacant.result: Built the client side of the premium subscription and put the product's first LLM features into production.
bechacant.responsibilities:
Product features in the PWA: one-on-one and one-against-many challenges with voting, a feed of posts and comments, notifications with push delivery, profiles and followers, an onboarding tutorial and a wallet with promo-code and referral rewards.

Mobile fixes: layouts that hold under Android's large font sizes, modal inputs kept clear of the on-screen keyboard, and shared links that open in the app instead of the browser.

Assistant panel: streamed answers and a choice of model and reasoning effort, tool calling and agent-style flows behind it, and every AI edit undoable as one step. Wrote the spec before the code and kept both in sync.

bechacant: Three challenge types with separate screens and statuses: every notification, shared link and expiring timer has to land on the right type and state, and the server's deadlines decide that state.

In-app purchases: the monthly subscription and restoring purchases go through a native bridge to the store, and every outcome (success, failure, cancellation, nothing to restore) maps to one status for the UI.
Keeping the model from inventing features: its context is built from the product's function list and docs, and the build fails as soon as the two drift apart.
eteam: Undo/redo for the whole app: widget moves, formulas, styles and other changes share one history, a change across several pages undoes as one step, and the history is kept in IndexedDB so it survives a reload.

Formula editor: references to widgets and cells are highlighted and autocompleted from page and widget names, errors show as you type and after server validation, and clicking a reference selects the widget on the page.
User-built pages: users configure tables, charts and text blocks on top of data from their own databases, and layout, alignment guides and PDF export work for any set of widgets.
